root_motivation: Grounding (truth-tier failures.md 2026-09-29 and 2026-09-28: 'signature in \'X-Hub-Signature-256\' did not match' from host.trigger.test, and 'host_quickstart: kind \'event\' is not registered' both nights). mcphost's kind="event" self-test demands a caller-computed HMAC over bytes (serde_json::to_vec re-serialization at src/hooks.rs:954) the caller never sees, while the sibling kind="webhook" self-test already self-signs (src/webhooks.rs:14-43). A shell-less agent either publishes a helper tool to compute HMAC or guesses -- the recipe integration-specialist-github-push-webhook-handler sits at 0.00 both nights. Fix: host.trigger.test self-signs when the caller doesn't supply the configured header, returns the exact signed bytes+headers for replay at the real URL, adds github/stripe verify presets, inlines a run's result from host.runs.list when it fits one part, and points host.quickstart/llms.txt at host.trigger.set instead of letting an agent guess triggers are a tool kind.
user_persona: Five (PRD User stories): a shell-less integration-specialist agent proving a GitHub push hook in <=4 calls; a workflow-orchestrator using verify:"github" instead of hand-assembling scheme/header/prefix; a rag_indexer agent reading a fired run's result from host.runs.list(trigger="event"); a SaaS operator whose fired runs keep end_user_subject; a first-run agent learning triggers are host.trigger.set(kind=...), not a tool kind.

acceptance_criteria.test: tests/mcphost_event_trigger_self_test_ac01_self_sign_when_no_headers.rs -- self-signs with no headers argument at all, checks the HMAC equality directly, then host.runs.wait to done.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given the same trigger, When host.trigger.test is called with headers: {"X-Hub-Signature-256": ""} or a wrong value, Then it fails signature_invalid with message "signature in 'X-Hub-Signature-256' did not match" and no run row is created.

scope: src/hooks.rs: host.trigger.test's kind="event" branch self-signs (sign_event helper factoring the hmac-sha256/hmac-sha1/token/stripe-style inverse of verify_event) when the caller's headers omit the trigger's configured verify header; returns signed:{body, headers}. A JSON-string body is signed byte-for-byte (no re-serialization); any other JSON value keeps the existing compact serde_json::to_vec. host.trigger.set(kind="event", verify: "github"|"stripe", secret: <name>) expands to the full verify object, tagging config_json with preset; host.trigger.get/list's tenant-facing verify now drops secret and preset entirely (preset surfaces as its own sibling field). EventCounters gains self_tests/self_test_signature_invalid cumulative counters.

src/runs.rs: host.runs.list(include_result?) inlines a terminal row's single-part result (attach_result_if_single_part); include_result=true clamps limit to 50 (down from 200); default false is byte-identical to today.

src/control.rs: host.quickstart(kind="schedule"|"event"|"webhook") fails unknown_kind with data.hint naming host.trigger.set; every authenticated quickstart response carries a one-sentence triggers pointer.

src/errors.rs: AppError::Structured{code:"unknown_kind",..}'s own jsonrpc_code mapped to INVALID_PARAMS (previously only the AppError::UnknownKind enum variant was), so quickstart's new hinted rejection carries the same wire error class as the pre-existing bare one.
src/handler.rs: host.trigger.set's verify/secret/dedupe_header schema descriptions document the preset form; host.runs.list's schema gains include_result and documents limit's new clamp.
www/llms.txt: First run walkthrough (after the Schedule step, before Claim) gains the one-sentence triggers pointer -- same sentence host.quickstart's response carries.

additional.byte_exact_body_is_string_passthrough_no: Open question 1 defaults to 'raw-slice for host.trigger.test only' (capturing the JSON-RPC argument's own original text via serde_json::value::RawValue) if unanswered, to make an OBJECT body's key order/whitespace byte-exact. No non-deferred AC actually tests object-body byte-exactness, though -- AC1 only checks the HMAC is self-consistent (computed over whatever bytes were sent), and AC9 (the one AC that does test exact-string preservation) passes body as a JSON STRING, whose content is already preserved character-for-character by ordinary JSON deserialization with no raw-slice capture needed. Resolved by the simpler mechanism requirement 6 already specifies: a string body is used verbatim; any other JSON value keeps the existing compact serde_json::to_vec re-serialization. This avoids a repo-wide serde_json preserve_order feature (technical considerations' own flagged risk: 'audit tests/ for order-sensitive assertions first') and a handler.rs-level RawValue plumbing change, neither of which any AC requires.
additional.stripe_preset_timestamp_header_names_the: Requirement 3's prose reads stripe -> {..., timestamp_header:"t", ...}, but verify_event's own hmac-* branch (src/hooks.rs) reads header_str(headers, ts_header) -- ts_header names an actual HTTP HEADER to read the whole t=,v1= value from, not a literal sub-field named 't' (the existing verify_event_stripe_style_* unit tests already construct their verify config with timestamp_header: "Stripe-Signature", the same name as header). No AC pins the stripe preset's exact stored shape (AC5 only tests the unknown- preset rejection). Resolved by setting timestamp_header equal to header ("Stripe-Signature") in the stripe preset, matching the mechanism that already exists rather than the PRD prose's literal 't'.
additional.verify_secret_stripped_for_every_event_t: AC4 only exercises the github preset, but the fix (dropping verify.secret from host.trigger.get/list's tenant-facing response) is applied uniformly to every kind="event" trigger, preset or hand-assembled object form alike -- narrowing it to preset-only would leave the exact same 'the response, on generation, returns the secret's plaintext value once' contract this module's own doc comment already promised never happens, just re-worded to 'except the secret's own name, sometimes' for no benefit; a single code path is simpler and matches AC4's intent (the secret must never be present) more literally than a preset-conditional one would.
additional.quickstart_hint_scoped_to_exactly_the_th: kind="message" is also a trigger word an agent could plausibly guess at host.quickstart, but requirement 5 and AC8 both name only schedule/event/webhook. Resolved by matching the literal enumeration -- message stays on the bare unknown_kind path (registered-kinds list only, no hint) rather than guessing the PRD's silence on it was an oversight.
additional.quickstart_text_is_the_structured_conten: AC8 says host.quickstart()'s TEXT must contain the sentence; this host's tools/call responses carry the JSON structured content as their own text content block too (tests/common/mod.rs's extract_structured falls back to parsing content[0].text when structuredContent is absent, and the two already carry the same JSON in this codebase's existing tool responses) -- so adding the sentence as a new top-level triggers field on the JSON response satisfies both structuredContent and the text block with one change, with no separate human-prose field needed.

five_whys_trace.q: Why did the recipe score 0.00 both nights?
five_whys_trace.a: The self-test rejected the persona's delivery, so no trigger=event run with the expected result ever existed for the scorer to read.

five_whys_trace.q: Why did host.trigger.test reject a signature the persona computed itself?
five_whys_trace.a: The persona signed its own JSON text (or guessed); mcphost verified over a canonical re-serialization (serde_json::to_vec of the parsed body) it never returned to the caller.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does the event kind demand a caller-supplied signature at all, when the sibling webhook kind self-signs?
five_whys_trace.a: hooks.rs's test() was built to drive the exact same verify-then-enqueue path handle_hook does, so real-sender rejections stay reproducible; webhooks.rs (built later) chose self-signing instead, and the two kinds' own self-tests were never reconciled.

five_whys_trace.q: Why wasn't this caught before a persona hit it in truth-tier?
five_whys_trace.a: Every existing Rust test computes the HMAC over serde_json::to_vec directly, from inside the same process -- no test modeled a caller that cannot run code and only sees the tool's own JSON schema.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does host.quickstart(kind="event") make the problem worse rather than just failing cleanly?
five_whys_trace.a: Its bare registered-kinds list (echo/http/python/wasm/chain, none named event) reads as 'this feature doesn't exist' rather than 'wrong tool, try host.trigger.set instead' -- costing the persona a full turn before it even reaches the self-test rejection above.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Should host.trigger.test's self-sign path apply to scheme: "token" (a plain shared secret, not a computed HMAC), or only the hmac-* schemes AC1/AC2 exercise directly?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Applied uniformly: sign_event's token branch returns the secret itself as the header value (verify_event's own token branch checks for exactly that), matching requirement 1's plain wording ('the configured scheme's signature', not 'the configured HMAC scheme's signature') rather than narrowing self-sign to the two schemes the P0 ACs happen to name.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does a github preset's default dedupe_header (X-GitHub-Delivery, open question 3) apply even when the caller already named their own dedupe_header?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No -- an explicit dedupe_header argument always wins; the preset default only fills in when the caller passed none at all, the same 'explicit beats default' precedent every other optional-argument default in this module already follows.
